critical_path.chain: Dcache set selects valid bits -> hit/fast response -> mem_completion_pending -> Load/MDU wb_dst selection -> IQ source match and candidate -> oldest grant[5] -> selected_ex2 / PRF and WB operand mux -> issue_b[30]
critical_path.next_bottleneck: Same-cycle Dcache completion-to-IQ wakeup/select-to-EX operand path, especially high-fanout grant and operand selection. Frontend next-PC/request paths are the next independent group. No additional RTL optimization performed after this result.

recovery_stage_comparison.definition: For every eventually committed control with EARLY_FETCH and FLUSH, measure DISPATCH of its next architecturally committed instruction minus that control EARLY_FETCH cycle. Same EX-resolution and rename-allocation stages in both versions. Killed controls and unrelated next commits are excluded. Sum is an exposure metric, not additive causal CPI or removable-cycle estimate.

checks.default_strict: Every architectural commit, global memory identity and selective ROB conservation; all annotated OoO/speculation/predictor/completion/recovery timing witnesses mandatory.
checks.small_nonpower: Every architectural commit and global memory/recovery identity; default-window timing witnesses explicitly disabled.
checks.current_rtl_legacy: Same current RTL with EARLY_RECOVERY=0 and PARALLEL_COMPLETION=0; every architectural commit and global memory/recovery identity checked; default-mechanism timing witnesses explicitly disabled.

qualification: Small non-power-of-two run skips default-window timing witnesses only; every architectural commit, memory identity, and selective ROB conservation remains checked.
CPU writeback faults inject second word 0x10004. True final-word R/B errors for 256-byte lines belong to the memory-unit evidence, not these CPU cases.
V4 legacy evidence uses the frozen V4 simulator, never the current V5 defaults.
Linux diagnostic-only run uses the root-owned official simulator; source identity is recorded by the parent official build evidence.

contracts.buffered_store_error: Fail-stop asynchronous diagnostic with original queued PC/instruction; younger retired instructions are not rolled back.
contracts.killed_load: Only younger uncommitted Loads are canceled; descriptors retain identity through drain and ROB/PRF reuse.
contracts.mmio: Wait for preceding descriptor responses and full cache dirty flush; no external exit after failed preceding Store.
contracts.default_cache_misses: One blocking miss; four ordered D-cache CPU credits.
contracts.timing: Course ideal-clock, no-parasitics synthesis estimate, not post-layout or silicon frequency.
